label: AMI Tutorial Object 5 : MISHA Fish Demo Object
description: This object displays a set of mulitspectral images created using the MISHA system, using Archipelago's integration of Mirador and custom IIIF Choice aware Manifest Template. This specialty View Mode and Twig Template combination was included in Archipelago's 2.2.0 Release in November 2026.|@|This object is using Archipelago's "Digital Object with IIIF Choice Manifest for Mirador" View Mode. You can review this View Mode by selecting the "Active Display Settings" tab above or navigating to '~/admin/structure/types/manage/digital_object/display/digital_object_with_iiif_choice_manifest'.|@|For this object, the CSV filed contained an already JSON-encoded value for "creator_lod"--so the role, name type, and label value were ingested directly without passing through further LoD reconciliation due to the logic present in the Advanced AMI Ingest Template. If you completed the Linked Data Reconciliation steps described in the AMI Tutorial documentation (for subjects only for this object), you will see that the subject data you reconcilied against various LoD endpoints has been mapped to LoD URIs, and will be showing in the Subjects block beside the main viewer.|@|Actual Object Description: This object provides a working demonstration of images captured using MISHA (Multispectral Imaging System for Historical Artifacts), a low-cost, open-source imaging platform developed by Rochester Institute of Technology’s Cultural Heritage Imaging Lab. More information about MISHA can be found here: https://www.rit.edu/chipr/misha . Use the \u0022Layers\u0022 slider (percentage) and visibility (eye icon) options on the left hand menu to review the different multispectral images available for this demo object. Read more about the IIIF Multiple Choice of Images in a Single View (Canvas) Cookbook recipe here: https://iiif.io/api/cookbook/recipe/0033-choice/
rights: The original illustration captured was sourced from the Dyer Arts Center Collection, a permanent collection of works by deaf/hard of hearing artists at RIT's NTID: https://www.rit.edu/ntid/. Please reach out to misha@rit.edu for any permissions or reuse related inquires.
